intro: A Portland singer of borderless Latin folk.
story: Edna Vazquez was born in Jalisco, Mexico, and settled in Portland, where she led the rock band No Passengers. A viral clip from a TV talent show led Luz Elena Mendoza of Y La Bamba to champion her, moving her from Mexican restaurants onto indie bills, and in 2015 she played Pickathon. From 2017 she toured as a special guest singer with Pink Martini, and an EP, Besame Mucho, with them followed. Te Esperaba, her own album, came out in the summer of 2025.
artist_reel_line: She toured with Pink Martini from 2017 and released Te Esperaba in 2025.

intro: A guitarist from the beginning of ska and reggae.
story: Ernest Ranglin was born on June 19, 1932, in Manchester, Jamaica, and from 1958 to 1965 was a staff guitarist at the Jamaica Broadcasting Corporation and a house arranger at Studio One. He arranged Millie Small's "My Boy Lollipop," the first million-selling Jamaican hit, and played on Bob Marley's earliest recordings. Told by Guitar World about ska, he said, "I invented the music, but not the word." Jamaica gave him its Order of Distinction in 1973, and the Order of Jamaica, the country's fifth highest honor, in 2021. He played Pickathon in 2015.
artist_reel_line: Jamaica gave him the Order of Jamaica in 2021.

story: Ex Hex formed in Washington, D.C., in 2013: Mary Timony, formerly of Helium and Wild Flag, with the bassist Betsy Wright and the drummer Laura Harris. Rips, their debut, came out on Merge on October 7, 2014, and placed 11th in the Village Voice's Pazz and Jop for 2014. NPR's first listen said there was enough energy on it to fuel a small country. They played Pickathon in 2015. It's Real came out in 2019, and they played a few East Coast club shows in late 2023.

Giant Sand began in Tucson in the late 1970s as Giant Sandworms, and its first album, Valley of Rain, came out in 1985. Thirty years later, on May 5, 2015, Heartbreak Pass came out on New West, and the band played Pickathon that summer. Howe Gelb said in 2016 that Heartbreak Pass seemed a good place to call it quits, on a high. In 2018 he revived the project with Returns to Valley of Rain, and he marked his seventieth birthday with an expanded Giant Giant Sand lineup in a hometown celebration at La Rosa.

Grandparents formed in Portland in 2009, after sharing a house with members of White Fang. Kids in the Alley came out on cassette on March 10, 2015, and Sincerely, Bagman followed that year on StrangeLight. They had played Project Pabst in 2014 with Modest Mouse and SXSW and Treefort in 2015, and a Slab Sessions video filmed at Pickathon ran in December 2015. Public records of the band end around 2016.

intro: A London trio of warm, off-kilter indie rock.
story: Happyness formed in south London in 2013 around Jon Allan, Benji Compston and Ash Kenazi, and by 2020 they were a duo. Stereogum named them a Band to Watch before Weird Little Birthday came out on Weird Smiling on June 16, 2014. Moshi Moshi and Bar/None reissued it in March 2015, with four bonus tracks, and PopMatters likened the American reissue to Pavement. They played Pickathon that summer. Write In came in 2017 and Floatr, their last major album, in 2020.

Jackson Boone emerged in Portland in late 2013, playing with a five-piece band, the Ocean Ghosts. His debut, Starlit, came out in 2014 on Wet Lettuce Records, produced by Riley Geare. Natural Changes followed on September 9, 2015, tracked over two weeks on the Oregon Coast, and Vortex counted him among the Portland acts with breakout sets at Pickathon that August. His last documented releases and hometown shows date to 2018 and 2019.

intro: A Portland gospel and soul voice.
story: Liz Vice was born in Portland on February 9, 1983, and never set out to sing; she first wanted acting and film, and came to music through a church gospel collective. Her debut, There's a Light, came out on September 25, 2015, and reached the R&B albums chart, and NPR Music said it challenges stereotypes about Christian music. She was at Pickathon that summer. Save Me came on June 1, 2018, on her own label, and NPR's First Listen praised its mindfulness. More recently she released the single The Call.

Summer Cannibals, a Portland band led by Jessica Boudreaux and named after a Patti Smith song, was called one of the city's best new bands by both Willamette Week and the Portland Mercury. No Makeup came out in 2013 and Show Us Your Mind in 2015 on their own New Moss label, and they played Pickathon that summer. Full of It followed on Kill Rock Stars on May 27, 2016, and they toured the country with the Thermals. After several years' hiatus, Boudreaux reunited the band to open for L7 in Portland, and has been recording new music.

intro: A rowdy Bay Area string band.
story: The Brothers Comatose started in 2008 on Haight Street in San Francisco, when the brothers Ben and Alex Morrison teamed with Phil Brezina. Ben says Alex's banjo playing sends him into a trance, hence the name. Songs from the Stoop came out in 2010 and Respect the Van, tracked live, on May 22, 2012. In 2015 they played Phil Lesh's Terrapin Crossroads and Pickathon, and City Painted Gold came in 2016. Golden Grass, an ode to San Francisco, followed in 2025 on Swamp Jam Records, and they returned to the farm in 2026.

The Easy Leaves are Kevin Carducci and Sage Fifield, a duo from Santa Rosa, California, who formed in 2008 with harmonies in the tradition of the Louvin and Everly brothers. A self-titled debut came in 2009, and American Times in 2012, with a video that reached CMT. They played Pickathon in 2015 and again in 2016. Their public performances taper off around 2020.

intro: A Texas Western swing trio with three fiddles.
story: The Quebe Sisters are three sisters from Burleson, Texas, who won fiddle contests as kids and learned Bob Wills swing from the champion fiddlers Joey and Sherry McKenzie. The band took off around 2003. Grace Quebe says they call it progressive western swing because they are continuing Wills's vision, not copying his sound. They played Connie Smith's Country Music Hall of Fame induction in 2012, toured Russia in 2013 and sang with Willie Nelson on a Bob Wills tribute in 2015, the year of their Pickathon set. They have won Western Swing Album of the Year from the Academy of Western Artists and the Western Music Association's Crescendo Award, and announced an open-ended hiatus after a farewell tour in 2023.

intro: A Cleveland indie-pop band of scruffy guitars.
story: Total Babes are a Cleveland indie-pop band. Heydays, an eight-track record, came out on Wichita on May 19, 2015, with Dylan Baldi of Cloud Nothings guesting on one track, and they played Pickathon that summer.
artist_reel_line: Heydays, an eight-track record, came out on Wichita in 2015.

story: Andy Cabic formed Vetiver in San Francisco in 2002, and it became tied to the early-2000s freak-folk scene. Tight Knit and The Errant Charm followed on Sub Pop in 2009 and 2011, and they played Pickathon in 2009, 2011 and 2015. Complete Strangers, their sixth album and the first on Easy Sound, was produced with Thom Monahan and came out on March 24, 2015, and reviews split. It has grown into a mellow, groove-oriented outfit.
artist_reel_line: Complete Strangers, their sixth album, came out in March 2015.

intro: A Michigan honky-tonker with Waylon in his bones.
story: Whitey Morgan and the 78's are an outlaw country band from Flint, Michigan, who took their name around 2007 and play upward of 300 shows a year, per Saving Country Music. Born, Raised & Live from Flint, recorded at the Machine Shop in Flint on November 25, 2011, came out on Bloodshot on December 2, 2014, and PopMatters and Glide both liked it. They came to Pickathon in 2011, 2012 and 2015. He has stayed on the road, booking club dates across North America through late 2026 and early 2027.

intro: A British folk-psych quartet of heavy, pastoral riffs.
story: Jack Sharp formed Wolf People in Bedford, England, in 2005, and they became the first British band signed to the US label Jagjaguwar. The 2010 debut, Steeple, was followed by Fain in April 2013. They played Pickathon in 2015 and returned in 2017, after Ruins in 2016. They announced an indefinite hiatus in January 2020.
